# Checkbox

*Class — [Control](declare-docs:Control) → [View](declare-docs:View) → [Node](declare-docs:Node)*

A boolean control. Its value is the
`checked` attribute; **`input` owns the value's destination** — by default the
destination is the checkbox itself, so it works standalone with zero wiring:

    mute: Checkbox [ label = "Mute" ]          … visible = { mute.checked }

Hand the value to its real owner by overriding `input` and constraining down:

    Checkbox [ label = "Mute", checked = { app.muted }, input(v: boolean) { app.muted = v } ]

`press()` never writes `checked` directly — it only delivers — so a constrained
checkbox never fights its constraint.

```declare
row: View [ x = 20, y = 20,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 8 ],
    mute: Checkbox [ label = "Mute" ],
    Text [ text = { mute.checked ? "muted" : "audible" } ]
    ]
```

## Attributes

| name | type | default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | number |  |  |
| `checked` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `label` | string | `""` |  |
| `size` | number | `0` |  |
| `height` | Length | `24` |  |
| `accessibilityRole` | none | button | toggle | checkbox | switch | radio | slider | progress | textField | link | image | heading | list | listItem | grid | row | cell | columnHeader | tabList | tab | tabPanel | menu | menuBar | menuItem | dialog | alertDialog | group | toolbar | region | status | listbox | option | tree | treeItem | radioGroup | combobox | separator | searchBox | spinButton | navigation | main | search | banner | complementary | `checkbox` |  |
| `accessibilityChecked` | boolean | `{ checked }` |  |
| `accessibilityLabel` | string | `{ provided("fieldLabel", "") }` |  |
| `width` | Length | `{ this.box.width + (label == "" ? 0 : 8 + this.cap.width) }` |  |
| `opacity` | number | `{ disabled ? (provided("theme").disabledOpacity) : 1 }` |  |

**`baseline`** — The baseline a row aligns this control by — the label's. Under `align = baseline` the
checkbox's caption sits on the same line as its neighbours; the box rides with it.

**`checked`** — Whether the box is ticked. Standalone it owns this and you read it back by name;
constrained (`checked = { app.muted }`) it needs an `input` override to go with it — **a
constraint with no `input` leaves the checkbox's own edit assigning to a constrained attribute,
which is refused at runtime.**

**`label`** — The text beside the box. `""` renders the box alone — the form for a checkbox inside a
table cell, where the column heading is the label.

**`size`** — The box's edge length. Defaults to the theme's figure, so a toolbar checkbox can shrink
to match its neighbours without a subclass.

**`accessibilityChecked`** — Follows `checked`; the visible label is the name.

**`accessibilityLabel`** — The caption of a `Field` around it, unless the use site names the checkbox; with neither, its
`label` is its name. A checkbox with no `label` — a task's in a list — is named at its use site:
`accessibilityLabel = :title`.

**`width`** — Content-sized: the box, then a gap and the label when there is one. A label-less checkbox is exactly its box, so a bare mark in a table cell reserves no phantom room.

**`opacity`** — Disabled dims the whole control — every part alike, never a recolour — to the theme's `disabledOpacity`, or 0.45 when the theme states none: the one place the number lives.

## Methods

- `focusShape()` — Rings the box alone, not the box-plus-label — the Radio rule, so a long label does not
drag a wide ring across the row.
- `input(v)` — **Where the value goes.** The default writes `checked`; override it and the checkbox
becomes a delivery channel for state you own (`input(v: boolean) { app.muted = v }`).
This is the one member to override when the value lives elsewhere.
- `press()` — Toggles by delivering the flipped value through `input` — **never by writing `checked`**,
which is what keeps a constrained checkbox from fighting its constraint. Called by a click and
by Space/Enter.

(`disabled = { app.muted }`) — it is ordinary derived state. Concrete controls also
dim themselves against `provided("theme").disabledOpacity`.

keyboard edge while a tabbed one does. What a `Pane` header's focus edge reads.

not nested as a child — a control is a leaf, and a name is the one form where authored

toolbar). Control only declares the attribute; the concrete control lays it out. A
**computed** name needs `use [ Name ]` to survive the build, since no static reference
reaches it. The name is read once, when the control is built: a name read from data gives
each row its own icon, but changing the name later does not swap the icon (see `IconHost`).

- `onClick()` — A click runs `press()` unless the control is disabled — so a control that overrides
`press()` is activated by pointer and keyboard alike without writing a handler. Override

- `openMenu()` — Opens `menu` anchored to this control, unless there is none or the control is disabled.
The seam a concrete control calls from its own `press()`.
- `press()` — **The activation seam — override this, not the handlers.** Pointer and keyboard both
land here — a click through `onClick`, Space and Enter through the keyboard — so one
override serves all three. The base opens `menu` when
there is one. A value control delivers through `input` from here and **never writes its

constraint.
- `focusShape()` — The focus silhouette the ring hugs, `{ x, y, w, h, rad }` in this control's own
