# Window

*Class — [View](declare-docs:View) → [Node](declare-docs:Node)*

A window inside a program: a raised surface with a title bar you drag it by and a button at
its end that closes it — and, when `resizable`, edges that resize it. It is the theme's
surface, hairline, rounding and shadow, as a dialog or a popover is, with the title bar the
same surface and a hairline under it.

It is also a world of its own. A menu, popover, dialog or sheet declared inside it opens
over it: above its content and past its edges, turning and scaling with it. A toast belongs
to the whole program and shows at the bottom of the App. Tab stays among the window's
controls; F6 moves to the next window, Shift-F6 back; a press inside it gives it the
keyboard, back on the control that last had focus there, and brings it to the front. A
dialog or sheet open in it holds back presses aimed at this window only — another window,
or what lies behind, still takes them. Esc closes it when focus is inside it and nothing
open inside it takes Esc first.

Its children go into its body, the pane below the title bar, and place themselves there as
in any view — give one a layout or a `padding` of its own. Whether it is open is state, by
the value pattern: `open` on its own, or `open = { … }` with `input` writing where your
state lives. Its `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` are its own to move and resize, so set them
as literals.

```declare
App [ width = 640, height = 360, fill = { provided("theme").background },
    notesOpen: boolean = true,
    Button [ x = 20, y = 316, label = "Show notes", disabled = { app.notesOpen },
        onClick() { app.notesOpen = true } ],
    Window [ x = 30, y = 30, width = 280, height = 190, title = "Settings",
        more: Menu [ items = { [ ({ id: "reset", label: "Reset" }), ({ id: "copy", label: "Copy settings" }) ] } ],
        View [ width = 100%, padding = 16,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 12 ],
            Checkbox [ label = "Show line numbers" ],
            Checkbox [ label = "Wrap long lines" ],
            Button [ label = "More", menu = { parent.parent.more } ]
            ]
        ],
    Window [ x = 330, y = 60, width = 280, height = 220, title = "Notes", resizable = true,
        open = { app.notesOpen }, input(v: boolean) { app.notesOpen = v },
        View [ width = 100%, padding = 16,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 10 ],
            TextInput [ width = 100%, placeholder = "Title" ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
```

### Without a frame

`frame = false` keeps the world and drops the frame: no surface, title bar, close button or
resize edges, and no bringing itself forward or closing on Esc — its fill, stroke, shadow
and rounding are yours, and so are moving, sizing and stacking it (`raise()` brings it to the
front). What a program with windows of its own design builds on — the Desktop app's are
these.

```declare
App [ width = 560, height = 260, fill = #E6E9EE,
    Window [ x = 40, y = 40, width = 240, height = 160, rotation = -4, frame = false, title = "Tilted",
        cornerRadius = 10, fill = white, shadow = { shadow(0, 6, 20, 0x00000033) },
        Text [ x = 16, y = 16, text = "A window of its own design" ],
        TextInput [ x = 16, y = 52, width = 200, accessibilityLabel = "Note" ]
        ]
    ]
```

## Attributes

| name | type | default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `title` | string | `""` |  |
| `closable` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `resizable` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `minWidth` | number | `200` |  |

**`frame`** — Whether the window draws its frame — surface, title bar, close button, resize edges — and
behaves as a framed window does: brought forward when pressed or reached, closed by Esc.
`true` by default; `false` leaves the window bare for a frame of your own.

**`title`** — The name in the title bar, and the window's name to a screen reader — give a frameless
window one too.

**`closable`** — Whether it has a close button and closes on Esc.

**`resizable`** — Whether its bottom and right edges and the corner between them resize it.

**`minWidth`** — The narrowest a resize makes it.

**`minHeight`** — The shortest a resize makes it.

**`titleBarHeight`** — The height of the title bar; the body starts below it. None without a frame.

**`open`** — Whether it is open. Constrain it to state of your own and override `input`, or leave it and
read it back.

**`overlays`** — The layer the overlays declared inside the window open in — its `layer`, read by them as
`provided("overlays")`.

**`width`** — 360 to begin with; a resize changes it.

**`height`** — 240 to begin with; a resize changes it.

**`accessibilityRole`** — `dialog`: a window that does not hold back the rest of the program.

**`accessibilityLabel`** — The `title`, so a screen reader names the window.

**`focusScope`** — `region`: Tab stays among the window's controls, and F6 moves between windows.

**`defaultplacement`** — `body`: its children go into the pane below the title bar (the whole window, without a
frame).

**`visible`** — Present while it is open.

**`fill`** — The theme's `surface`; none without a frame.

**`stroke`** — A hairline in the theme's `line`; none without a frame.

**`cornerRadius`** — The theme's dialog rounding; none without a frame.

**`shadow`** — The theme's dialog shadow; none without a frame.

## Events

- `onPointerDown()` — A press inside the window, on nothing that takes it, gives the window the keyboard — and a
framed one comes to the front.

## Methods

- `input(v)` — **Where an opening or a closing goes**, receiving the new open state. The default writes
`open`; override it to own the destination.
- `close()` — Closes it, through `input(false)` — what the close button and Esc do.
- `show()` — Opens it, through `input(true)`, and brings it to the front.
- `holdsFocus()` — Whether focus is inside the window now, in a program it hosts included.
- `enter()` — Gives the window the keyboard: focus goes back to the control that last had it inside the
window, else to the first. What a press inside the window does; a program's own way of
bringing a window to the front calls it too.
- `bringForward()` — Brings it in front of the windows beside it — its siblings that are windows — and keeps it
beneath whatever its parent holds above them. A press in a framed window, focus arriving in
it and `show()` all call it.
