# Types and functions

*The shared vocabulary every `{ }` body can name. The scaffold declares all of it into
each program's check block, so it is typechecked for your code exactly as for the
standard library's.*

Beyond the tree, a bare name in a body may be one of three things, the same on every
renderer: an **ES built-in** (`Math`, `JSON`, `Date`, `Promise`, `Map`, …); one of the
**host chores declared below** (timers, `console`, `fetch` and the `URL` family) — each
with the one narrow shape it has everywhere Declare runs; or a **runtime service**
(`Focus`, `Keys`, `Themes`, `afterSettle`). Nothing else: `document`, `window`,
`localStorage`, `process` are the host's, and the compiler refuses each by name with the
Declare way beside it. A capability the language lacks arrives through an `external`
attribute the host supplies, never through a bare global. A body is synchronous — there
is no `await`; a value the screen derives from is a `DataSource`.

## `Draw` — what a `draw(d)` method receives

`draw(d: Draw)` is an ordinary method a view defines to paint itself. `View` calls it from a
constraint of its own (`drawing = { record(draw) }` — the View page), so it runs on invalidation
and re-runs when what it *read* changes, **never per frame** — the rule every method has when a
constraint calls it. So a drawing composes with attributes and constraints instead of escaping
them — `ink`, `width` and state are ordinary reads, and changing one re-records. What it records
is a display list every renderer paints.

This is how the library draws every mark a font cannot give it: a `Checkbox`'s tick and the
whole `Icon` set are recorded paths, not glyphs. Author an icon in a 16×16 box and scale it
inside the body (see `Icon`); **never animate a drawing's size** — reading size inside `draw`
makes the recording size-dependent, so an animated size re-records and reallocates its backing
canvas every frame.

```declare-fragment
draw(d: Draw) {
    d.fillStyle = provided("theme").accent
    d.beginPath()
    d.arc(width / 2, height / 2, 6, 0, Math.PI * 2, false)
    d.fill()
    }
```

`d.w` / `d.h` are the view's own size, for a drawing that sizes itself. Reading one is
what opts a drawing into re-recording when the view resizes — a body that never mentions
them never pays for the resize. (There is no `d.x`/`d.y`: a recording's origin IS the
view's top-left, so they could only be 0.)

# Theme tokens

*The vocabulary the standard library reads off the `theme` provided value. Measured from
the library sources, so it cannot drift from what the classes actually consult.*

A `theme` is a plain record, a **provided value**: set it high in the tree and every
descendant reads it with `provided("theme")` until one overrides it. Start from a preset and
spread to change a token — **an empty record is not a theme**, because the library reads
specific names:

```declare-fragment
theme = { app.dark ? SanFranciscoDark : SanFrancisco },     // on the App
theme = { { ...provided("theme"), accent: 0xCC3333 } }       // override one token below
```

Presets, each with a light record and a `…Dark` companion: [`Cupertino`](declare-docs:Cupertino) · [`MountainView`](declare-docs:MountainView) · [`Redmond`](declare-docs:Redmond) · [`SanFrancisco`](declare-docs:SanFrancisco).

## Required — the contract

**15 tokens are read bare**, with no fallback. A record missing one of these
breaks the classes that read it, which is why a theme is built from a preset rather than
from scratch.

| token | read by |
|---|---|
| `accent` | button, checkbox, datagrid, datepicker, focusring, gauge, … |
| `accentHovered` | button, datepicker |
| `accentPressed` | button, datepicker |
| `accentTextColor` | button, checkbox, datepicker, menu |
| `control` | accordion, button, checkbox, gauge, progressbar, segmented, … |
| `controlCornerRadius` | accordion, appearanceswitch, breadcrumb, button, card, checkbox, … |
| `controlHovered` | appearanceswitch, button, datepicker, disclosure, segmented, stepper, … |
| `controlPressed` | appearanceswitch, button, datepicker, disclosure, segmented, stepper, … |
| `controlSelected` | accordion, button, menubar, switch, table, tree |
| `focusRingStyle` | focusring |
| `line` | card, checkbox, datagrid, datepicker, dialog, divider, … |
| `surface` | card, datagrid, datepicker, dialog, focusring, menu, … |
| `text` | accordion, appearanceswitch, breadcrumb, button, datepicker, dialog, … |
| `textFaint` | window |
| `textMuted` | accordion, appearanceswitch, breadcrumb, checkbox, combobox, datagrid, … |

## Optional — the tuning surface

**83 tokens have a default.** Every provided theme is laid over the library's
defaults record (`ThemeDefaults`), so a theme states only what it changes; a token whose
default is another token (`trackFill` is `control` unless stated) is read with `??`.
These are what a city preset reaches for to change platform character — button geometry,
menu material, focus-ring behaviour, dialog arrangement.

children.name: Enums
children.label: Reference
children.doc:
# Enums

*The language's fixed token sets — write the token itself, never a CSS-style value. Each has a page of its own in the reference (`type/<Name>`), with where it is used.*

**Backface** — `visible` · `hidden`

What a view shows once a rotation turns it more than 90° about X or Y. `hidden`
takes the turned-away face out of the picture **and out of hit-testing**, so a
pointer passes through to whatever is behind it; `visible` keeps painting the
mirrored face.

**Blend** — `normal` · `multiply` · `screen` · `overlay` · `darken` · `lighten` · `colorDodge` · `colorBurn` · `hardLight` · `softLight` · `difference` · `exclusion` · `hue` · `saturation` · `color` · `luminosity` · `plusLighter`

The W3C blend modes, in camelCase, naming how a view lands against what has
already painted beneath it. The operator is not a filter on the view: it reaches
down to the nearest **isolating** ancestor, so what a `multiply` chip blends with
depends on where the isolation is, not on how deeply it is nested. `normal` is no
blending at all, and the value every view has until one is named.

**Scaling** — `smooth` · `pixelated`

How a view's images and drawings look when they are shown larger or smaller. `smooth`
blends neighbouring pixels, which suits photographs and an ordinary interface under a
zoom. `pixelated` shows every pixel as a solid block, so pixel art stays sharp. A view's
whole subtree follows its setting.

**Scrolls** — `none` · `y` · `x` · `both`

Which axes of interior overflow a view scrolls. Overflow along a declared axis
becomes scroll range; overflow along any other axis is simply out of frame,
because a scroller clips to its box either way. The value is a token **string** in
a `{ }` body, so compare it explicitly — `"none"` is truthy, and a bare truth test
says every view scrolls.

**Claim** — `both` · `x` · `y`

The axis a declared drag takes for itself. `both` (the default) gives the drag the
whole gesture; `x` or `y` leaves the other axis to the enclosing scroller, so a
horizontal column-drag and a vertical page scroll can share one finger. It
**scopes** a drag that already exists and never creates one — a view with no
pointer handler ignores it.

**ScrollAnchor** — `content` · `end` · `none`

What a scroller keeps still while its content changes size. `content` keeps the
reader's place: the view at the top edge stays where it is, and a pane at its very
start stays at its start. `end` is for a pane read from the bottom, such as a
terminal or a build's output: at its end it stays at the end as content grows, and away
from the end it keeps the reader's place. `none` leaves the offset alone.

**Direction** — `inherit` · `ltr` · `rtl` · `auto`

The direction a view's text runs in, and what it holds: `ltr`, `rtl`, or `auto` (from the
first strong letter of the text); `inherit`, the default, takes the nearest ancestor's.
A right-to-left paragraph is laid out from the right — its lines start there unless its
`textAlign` says otherwise — and a field types from the right.

**OutsidePress** — `none` · `dismiss` · `dismissAndDeliver` · `block` · `ignore`

What a press aimed past an open overlay does: `dismiss` (the overlay closes; the press goes
no further — a menu), `dismissAndDeliver` (it closes; the press goes on — a popover), `block`
(the press goes nowhere; the overlay stays — a dialog), `ignore` (the press goes on as if the
overlay were not there — a toast). `none` is every ordinary view.

**ScrollBelow** — `none` · `block` · `allow` · `dismiss`

What a scroll aimed past an open overlay does: `block` (nothing behind it scrolls — a menu,
a dialog), `allow` (it goes on — a popover, a toast), `dismiss` (the overlay closes and the
scroll goes on — a tooltip). `none` is every ordinary view.

**FocusScope** — `none` · `stop` · `capture` · `region` · `modal`

What Tab does at a view's edge. `none`: its stops are its parent's. `stop`: it is one Tab stop
and the arrows move inside (a radio group, a list). `capture`: Tab walks in and through its
stops (an entry form). `region`: one stop from outside, a cycle of its own inside, left with
F6 (a window, a pane). `modal`: Tab wraps inside and never leaves (a dialog).

**AccessibilityRole** — `none` · `button` · `toggle` · `checkbox` · `switch` · `radio` · `slider` · `progress` · `textField` · `link` · `image` · `heading` · `list` · `listItem` · `grid` · `row` · `cell` · `columnHeader` · `tabList` · `tab` · `tabPanel` · `menu` · `menuBar` · `menuItem` · `dialog` · `alertDialog` · `group` · `toolbar` · `region` · `status` · `listbox` · `option` · `tree` · `treeItem` · `radioGroup` · `combobox` · `separator` · `searchBox` · `spinButton` · `navigation` · `main` · `search` · `banner` · `complementary`

What a view is to assistive technology — the closed vocabulary every platform's accessibility
API shares, so a program is written for none of them in particular. Each word is a contract: it
names the facts the role reads and the methods its actions call, and the compiler holds a class
that declares it to them. `none` is transparent — the view is read as part of its parent.

**AccessibilityLive** — `off` · `polite` · `assertive`

How a change to a live view is announced. `off`: it is not. `polite`: at the next pause, without
interrupting. `assertive`: at once, interrupting what is being read — for what cannot wait.

**AccessibilitySort** — `none` · `ascending` · `descending`

Which way the column a `columnHeader` heads is sorted, as a screen reader says it with the
header's name: `none` (not the sorted column), `ascending` or `descending`.

**Edges** — `safe` · `cover`

How an app meets the device's **own** chrome — a notch, a home-indicator bar.
`safe` keeps the app inside the safe region and every `safe*` inset then reads 0,
because there is nothing left to handle. `cover` is the edge-to-edge opt-in: the
box extends under the system chrome and the insets carry real numbers, which is
what pinned chrome needs to place itself.

**FontWeight** — `thin` · `extralight` · `light` · `regular` · `normal` · `medium` · `semibold` · `bold` · `extrabold` · `black`

The named weights, and a **number from 1 to 1000 is the same attribute** — the
keywords are the names of the hundreds. That is what puts a variable font's weight
axis in reach at any point between the names — `fontWeight = 480` is as legal as
`fontWeight = regular`, and there is no second attribute to learn for it.

**TextAlign** — `left` · `center` · `right`

Horizontal alignment of wrapped lines inside the run's own width. It only means
anything once the run **has** a width to align within — a `Text` that sizes itself
to its content is already exactly as wide as its longest line, so every value
looks the same.

**TextTransform** — `none` · `uppercase` · `lowercase` · `capitalize`

Reshapes the painted glyphs **without changing `text`**: selection, find-in-page
and `$data` all see the original string, exactly as CSS `text-transform` behaves.
The measurer shapes the transformed glyphs, so an `uppercase` run still wraps
correctly at its real width on every renderer.

**Numerals** — `normal` · `lining` · `oldstyle`

The **shape** of the digits in a face that carries more than one set. `normal` is
whatever the face does by itself, and faces differ on that, so it is worth naming
the one you want rather than relying on the default. A face with a single set
ignores the value, silently and correctly.

**NumeralWidth** — `normal` · `tabular` · `proportional`

The **advance** of the digits, which is a different question from their shape.
`tabular` gives every digit the same width, so a column of figures lines up and a
counter does not jitter as it counts; `proportional` lets each digit take its
natural width and reads better in prose. `normal` defers to the face, and faces
disagree about which of the two that is.

**Stretch** — `none` · `width` · `height` · `both` · `cover` · `contain`

How a bitmap fills a box whose size differs from its natural size. The axis values
— `width`, `height`, `both` — **distort by design**; the aspect-preserving fits
never do: `contain` puts the whole picture in the box and letterboxes the
remainder, `cover` fills the box and crops the overflow. `none` paints at natural
size. Both fits center the picture until `FitAlign` says otherwise.

**FitAlign** — `start` · `center` · `end`

Which end of the box an aspect-preserving fit keeps, one axis at a time. It is
read only by `contain` (which letterboxes on one axis) and `cover` (which crops on
one) — under a distorting stretch there is nothing left over to align, and the
value is ignored.

**Purpose** — `text` · `name` · `email` · `username` · `password` · `newPassword` · `oneTimeCode` · `tel` · `url` · `digits` · `decimal` · `cardNumber` · `cardName` · `cardExpiry` · `cardCode` · `addressLine1` · `addressLine2` · `city` · `region` · `postalCode` · `country`

What a text field holds — an email address, a password, a card number, a line of an
address — said once on `TextInput.purpose`, so the platform can help: autofill and
password managers recognise the field, a phone brings up the keyboard that suits it,
and a password is hidden. `text`, the default, says nothing.

**EditorJudgeOn** — `edit` · `leave`

When a field first says what is wrong with its draft (`Editor.judgeOn`): `edit` at every
edit, `leave` once the field has been left — or `judge()` asked — and at every edit after.

**Credentials** — `omit` · `sameOrigin` · `include`

Whether a request carries cookies, TLS client certificates and authentication
headers. These are the Fetch API's three modes as tokens, so `sameOrigin` is the
camelCase spelling of the wire's `same-origin`. `include` is the only one that
reaches another origin, and it works **only** when that origin's CORS response
names your origin back — a wildcard `*` cannot combine with it.

**Process** — `sequential` · `simultaneous`

Whether the members of an `AnimatorGroup` run one after another or all at once. It
is the group's own control — nothing else in the language reads it — and it is
what makes a group more than a list of animators started together.

**Tick** — `frame` · `second` · `minute` · `hour` · `day`

How often a `Time` fires, from the display's own rate up to a calendar boundary.
The calendar tiers aim at the **boundary** — aligned and drift-free, so an
hour-ticking clock changes on the hour rather than an hour after it started —
while `frame` follows the display and is the one to reach for when something is
being animated rather than counted. A number instead of a token is a period in
milliseconds — `tick = 30000` — counted from when the `Time` starts, for a repeating
job that is not about the time of day.

**FontLate** — `swap` · `keep`

What a face that finishes loading **after** the text is already painted does to
text already on screen. `swap` changes to the real face — one redraw, and the
usual answer. `keep` leaves the fallback in place for the rest of the run, which
is how a reflow mid-read is avoided; a face kept this way reports `loaded = false`
for the life of the run.

**StreamStatus** — `closed` · `connecting` · `open` · `retrying` · `failed`

A live connection's lifecycle as one read-only fact, the same shape a `DataSource`'s `loaded` / `loading` / `failed` facts
has for a fetch. `retrying` is the one worth planning for: it covers both the
platform's own recovery and a declared retry waiting to re-dial, and it is the
difference between a stream that is coming back and `failed`, which is not.

**Motion** — `linear` · `ease` · `easeIn` · `easeOut` · `easeBoth` · `sineIn` · `sineOut` · `sineBoth` · `quadIn` · `quadOut` · `quadBoth` · `cubicIn` · `cubicOut` · `cubicBoth` · `quartIn` · `quartOut` · `quartBoth` · `quintIn` · `quintOut` · `quintBoth` · `expoIn` · `expoOut` · `expoBoth` · `circIn` · `circOut` · `circBoth` · `backIn` · `backOut` · `backBoth` · `laszloIn` · `laszloOut` · `laszloBoth`

The shape of an interpolation over its duration: which fraction of the travel has
been covered at each fraction of the time. Read a token as a family plus a
direction — `In` bends at the start, `Out` at the end, `Both` at each end with the
fastest part in the middle.

The polynomial families bend progressively harder in this order: `sine`, `quad`,
`cubic`, `quart`, `quint`, `expo`, `circ` — so `quadOut` is a gentle settle and
`expoOut` a sharp one. `easeIn`, `easeOut` and `easeBoth` are the `quad` family
under an older set of names, and `ease` on its own is the CSS default curve, not a
member of any family. `back` overshoots the target and comes back, which reads as
weight. `laszlo` is the one curve that reads how far the animator is actually
travelling, so its bend adapts to the distance rather than being fixed by the
token. `linear` is no easing at all.

**Axis** — `x` · `y`

Which way an arrangement runs. It is a **bare token, not a string** — `axis = x`
names the axis, and the `x` here is unrelated to the position attribute of the same
name. Every stacking layout takes one, and `y` is the house default, so a column is
what you get by naming no axis at all.

**Justify** — `start` · `center` · `end` · `fill`

How a finished row sits along the direction of flow. `start`, `center` and `end`
move the row; `fill` does not — it spreads the row's slack into the gaps between
its children, so every full row ends flush. As in justified text, the **last row
stays at `start`** under `fill`, and a row holding one child has no gap to widen.

**CrossAlign** — `none` · `start` · `center` · `end` · `baseline`

Where a laid child sits across the flow — `y` on a row, `x` on a stack. `none`
leaves the cross placement to the child, which is what lets an ordinary
`y = center` keep working; `start | center | end` place every child for you. Pick
`baseline` only where each child can report one: a `Text` does by itself, and a
composite must **declare** which of its parts carries it.

children.label: Reference
children.doc:
# Compile flags

*Modifiers, one set of names and values, written `name = value` in a program's `defaultFlags`, `?name=value` on a URL, and `--name=value` to `declarec`.*

| flag | what it does | default |
|---|---|---|
| `render` | render through managed DOM or a single <canvas>; unset, the program's flags decide | `dom` |
| `crawler` | embed the crawled document in the host page, for crawlers; unset, the program's flags decide | `false` |
| `kernel` | the reactive kernel a build carries: the C kernel as WebAssembly, or the JavaScript one (a smaller download); unset, the program's flags decide | `wasm` |
| `accessibility` | carry the accessibility layer: what screen readers and the platform's accessibility API are given, the accessibility warnings, and the accessibility settings an app can read; unset, the program's flags decide | `true` |

children.name: Diagnostics
children.label: Reference
children.doc:
# Diagnostic codes

*Every compiler diagnostic carries a `DECLARE####` code, and its message names the fix. `npx declare-help DECLARE4001` answers one code in full.*

## Syntax

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `DECLARE1001` | the parser rejected a token or shape |
| `DECLARE1002` | a value body wrapped whole in parentheses — { expr } says it (hint) |

## Structure

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `DECLARE2000` | structural error (unclassified) |
| `DECLARE2001` | unknown class tag |
| `DECLARE2002` | a name is declared more than once |
| `DECLARE2003` | a member is placed where its node-kind forbids it |
| `DECLARE2004` | a name violates the member namespace |
| `DECLARE2005` | a Spring drives an attribute its view also binds — the target belongs in the Spring's to |
| `DECLARE2006` | a class declares an accessibilityRole whose contract it does not meet |
| `DECLARE2007` | accessibilityRole written as a { } value — a role is a word, fixed for the view's life |

## Values and types

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `DECLARE3000` | type/value error (unclassified) |
| `DECLARE3001` | a value does not fit its attribute's type |
| `DECLARE3002` | a percent with no axis to resolve against |
| `DECLARE3003` | a malformed datapath |
| `DECLARE3004` | an attribute is set twice |
| `DECLARE3005` | a text field's size sits under the iOS focus-zoom line (warning) |
| `DECLARE3006` | a datapath { } is a literal — a fresh value no Dataset holds |

## Names and scope

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `DECLARE4000` | name-resolution error (unclassified) |
| `DECLARE4001` | a bare name resolves to nothing in scope |
| `DECLARE4002` | a bare name shadows an outer member (warning) |
| `DECLARE4003` | a body writes a script { } variable (a body holds a copy — state lives on a node) |
| `DECLARE4004` | a body names a host global (document, window, process, …) — the Declare way is named |
| `DECLARE4005` | a bare enum token inside { } — the quoted form is named |
| `DECLARE4006` | a per-frame Time's onTick ignores dt — polling, not integration (warning) |
| `DECLARE4007` | a { } reads the ambient clock (Date.now(), new Date()) — a stopped clock (warning) |
| `DECLARE4008` | no 'shows' name matches the initial location — every screen starts hidden (warning) |
| `DECLARE4010` | a class is named like a rich-text tag — that tag builds this class inside content (warning) |
| `DECLARE4011` | a constraint centers a box by hand — x = center says it (hint) |
| `DECLARE4012` | an Animator nothing ever starts — no 'started', no start() call (warning) |
| `DECLARE4013` | a press() override on a Button — the click runs onClick, not this (warning) |
| `DECLARE4019` | a method named on… that answers no event of its class — an ordinary method (warning) |
| `DECLARE4016` | a Control with no accessibilityRole (warning) |
| `DECLARE4017` | a view whose role needs a name has none (warning) |
| `DECLARE4018` | a drawn, focusable view with no accessibilityRole (warning) |
| `DECLARE4020` | a control inside a control — interactive inside interactive (warning) |
| `DECLARE4021` | a view clipped to zero size to hide what a screen reader still reads (warning) |
| `DECLARE4022` | a control that shows it is chosen and reports no state (warning) |
| `DECLARE4023` | rowIndex read on a view that is not replicated — its own, never the row's (warning) |
| `DECLARE4024` | a write to a dataset that computes its value with contents (warning) |
| `DECLARE4025` | a constraint whose decisions are nested three deep, or one condition with four or more parts (warning) |
| `DECLARE4014` | afterDelay() in a { } value — a value computes and never waits |
| `DECLARE4015` | a class, schema, theme or style takes a name TypeScript's standard library or Declare's own types declare |

## Files and includes

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `DECLARE5000` | include/module error (unclassified) |
| `DECLARE5001` | two included files declare the same class |
| `DECLARE5002` | an include path cannot be found |
| `DECLARE5003` | an included library has a tree root |

## Type checking

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `DECLARE6000` | typecheck error (unclassified) |
| `DECLARE6001` | a { } body fails the TypeScript typecheck |

## Constraints

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `DECLARE7000` | constraint dependency error (unclassified) |
| `DECLARE7001` | a { } constraint cannot be statically analyzed (residue) |

children.name: Requests
children.label: Reference
children.doc:
# Request types

*What a program URL returns. One request per URL; with no request key, a program runs. A request combines with the compile flags — `?viewer=edit&render=canvas`.*

| request | URL | what it returns |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | *(no key)* | boot and run the program — what an ordinary link to a `.declare` file does |
| `build` | `?build` | the self-contained production package `declarec` makes, served as a directory |
| `reader` | `?viewer` | Declare Viewer's Reader: the source highlighted, its block comments rendered as prose |
| `source` | `?viewer=source` | the Viewer showing the source verbatim |
| `edit` | `?viewer=edit` | the Viewer's workbench: the source in an editor, the running program below it |
| `sizes-tab` | `?viewer=sizes` | the Viewer's Sizes tab: what the production package is made of and what each part weighs, every file and runtime module with what brought it aboard |
| `file` | `?file` | the raw source file as plain text — what an `include` or `curl` reads |
| `segments` | `?segments` | the Reader's data alone — the highlighted segments as JSON, for tooling |
| `extract` | `?extract` | the HTML a crawler reads: the program's content at its first frame |
| `sizes` | `?sizes` | what the production package is made of and what each part weighs, as JSON — on the dev server, as `?build` is |
